newsitem.title: USA: DII Group sees EPS hit by orders slowdown.
newsitem.headline: DII Group sees EPS hit by orders slowdown.

text.p: DII Group Inc said Sunday it expects a slowdown in orders at its DOVatron International unit to cut its second-half revenues by about $40 million and fully-diluted earnings per share by some $0.35.
Analysts' consensus earnings estimates for the company were $0.58 for the third quarter, $0.74 for the fourth quarter, and $2.41 for the year, according to First Call Research Network.

DII said that with the exception of a Hewlett-Packard Co order, there have been delays in the timing of production for orders from new customers at various contract electronics manufacturing (CEM) facilities around the world.

"These new customers, which were announced during the company's second quarter analysts call, are not ramping up as fast as previously expected for the fourth quarter of 1996, and are now expected to reach full volume production in the first quarter of 1997," DII said in a statement.
The company said its third quarter revenues will be slightly less than second quarter revenues on a pro forma merged company basis.
It added that fourth quarter revenues should increase sequentially by about 10 percent.
DII completed its buy of Orbit Semiconductor in August.

"Although DOVatron divisions are experiencing the effects of a general industry slowdown in the second half of 1996, we are confident that they will return to historical growth rates in both revenues and profits in 1997," DII said.

"Based upon the feedback from our customers, and our linked marketing initiative with all DII companies, the DII Group's operating plan for 1997 appears to be in-line with analysts' earnings consensus," it added.
The company said its higher-margin businesses exceeded their operating plans in the first half of 1996 and were able to off-set some order softness experienced by DOVatron.

"However, these specialty businesses have returned to planned operating profit levels in the third quarter," DII said, adding that earnings from its non-CEM businesses are not expected to off-set DOVatron's softness in the second half.
DII's shares fell 3-1/8 to 23 on Friday.
